phases.name: Define boundaries and the trust contract
phases.description: Separate the brief's outcomes from deployment assumptions, then establish the tenant-facing control plane and its durable policy state.

phases.name: Ingest and normalize multi-cloud evidence
phases.description: Bring AWS, Azure, and GCP billing exports and resource-usage evidence into a versioned, normalized cost ledger without conflating estimates with finalized charges.

phases.name: Attribute spend and detect opportunities
phases.description: Derive team/service views, infer missing ownership cautiously, and detect anomalies and workload patterns from cost and utilization evidence.

phases.name: Optimize resources, commitments, and forecasts
phases.description: Generate evidence-backed rightsizing and commitment scenarios, then forecast by team and service while preserving uncertainty and approval boundaries.

phases.name: Govern recommendations and expose outcomes
phases.description: Evaluate recommendations against versioned policies, make any cloud-side action explicitly opt-in, and expose auditable results to the teams that own the spend.

steps.phase: Define boundaries and the trust contract
steps.title: Keep brief facts separate from design assumptions
steps.content: Provided by the brief: analyze cloud spending across providers; detect idle and underutilized resources; recommend rightsizing; optimize reserved-instance and savings-plan coverage; forecast by team and service; identify cost anomalies; automate cost-governance policies; and provide allocation/showback/chargeback. Its stated targets are recommendation accuracy above 90%, anomaly detection within 1 hour, AWS/Azure/GCP billing support, 10k+ resources across accounts, and forecast accuracy within 10%. These are acceptance targets, not proven results. Design assumptions (not supplied facts): each provider can deliver billing exports plus sufficiently fresh usage or estimated-cost signals; organizations connect accounts explicitly; the product proposes purchases and changes by default, with cloud-side execution only after an administrator opts in; forecast horizon, granularity, and accuracy definitions must be agreed with product owners. React, JWT, PostgreSQL, Flink, S3 as a central landing choice, Snowflake, Prometheus/Grafana, Scikit-learn, and XGBoost are replaceable implementation examples selected for the diagram, not facts or requirements from the brief. Do not treat any assumption as a requirement.

steps.phase: Define boundaries and the trust contract
steps.title: Give teams a cost workspace
steps.content: The workspace is an inferred product surface for reviewing allocations, recommendations, anomalies, and forecasts; it is not an additional scale or availability requirement.

component.label: FinOps Workspace
component.description: Tenant-aware workspace for finance and engineering teams to inspect allocated spend, evidence-backed recommendations, anomalies, and forecasts.

properties.purpose: Tenant-aware workspace for finance and engineering teams to inspect allocated spend, evidence-backed recommendations, anomalies, and forecasts.

component.highlightReason: Make cost decisions reviewable by the teams accountable for the spend rather than presenting an opaque savings score.

steps.phase: Define boundaries and the trust contract
steps.title: Protect the public application boundary
steps.content: Authenticate organization and team access before exposing billing detail or accepting policy changes. JWT is a replaceable implementation choice, not a brief requirement.

component.label: Authenticated Cost API
component.description: Validates tenant identity, request shape, TLS, and per-tenant rate limits before forwarding workspace requests.

properties.purpose: Validates tenant identity, request shape, TLS, and per-tenant rate limits before forwarding workspace requests.

component.highlightReason: Cost and allocation data are sensitive; identity and tenant scoping must be enforced before reads and writes.

steps.phase: Define boundaries and the trust contract
steps.title: Workspace requests enter through the authenticated boundary
steps.content: Keep browser credentials and tenant context at the gateway; never let a client select another organization's account IDs without server-side authorization.

connection.label: Authenticated workspace requests
connection.description: Send scoped report, recommendation, forecast, and policy-review requests over TLS.

steps.phase: Define boundaries and the trust contract
steps.title: Add the tenant-scoped application service
steps.content: Keep product APIs, saved views, review workflows, and authorization checks behind one service boundary; split it only when measured ownership or load requires it.

component.label: Cost Platform API
component.description: Tenant-scoped API for cost views, forecast and recommendation retrieval, policy configuration, and approval records.

properties.purpose: Tenant-scoped API for cost views, forecast and recommendation retrieval, policy configuration, and approval records.

component.highlightReason: Separate the user-facing contract from provider ingestion and optimization jobs so retries or backfills do not block interactive review.

steps.phase: Define boundaries and the trust contract
steps.title: Forward validated requests to the platform API
steps.content: The API rechecks tenant permissions for every data path; gateway authentication alone does not authorize a specific account, team, or policy mutation.

connection.label: Tenant-scoped API calls
connection.description: Pass validated identity and request context for authorization, reporting, and review operations.

steps.phase: Define boundaries and the trust contract
steps.title: Persist control-plane state separately from cost facts
steps.content: Store tenant/account mappings, versioned policies, approvals, recommendation status, and audit references here. Large time-series cost facts belong in the analytical store, not this OLTP database.

component.label: Policies, Reviews & Audit Store
component.description: Encrypted OLTP state for tenant/account mapping, versioned governance policies, recommendation review status, approvals, and audit references.

properties.purpose: Encrypted OLTP state for tenant/account mapping, versioned governance policies, recommendation review status, approvals, and audit references.

component.highlightReason: Keep approval and policy history durable and tenant-scoped without putting the high-volume analytical ledger into an OLTP access pattern.

steps.phase: Define boundaries and the trust contract
steps.title: Persist policy and review transitions
steps.content: Version every policy change and keep approver, scope, timestamp, and before/after state so a later chargeback or automated action can be explained.

connection.label: Versioned control-plane state
connection.description: Read and write tenant-scoped account mappings, policy versions, approvals, and recommendation review records.

steps.phase: Define boundaries and the trust contract
steps.title: Choose a safe starting mode
steps.content: Start with explainable recommendations and policy enforcement before allowing provider-side mutations. The brief asks for automated governance, but does not grant authority to purchase commitments or resize production resources.

decision.question: What should the platform do when a recommendation meets a configured policy?
decision.chosen: Persist the recommendation and policy result; permit cloud-side changes only for explicitly opted-in, scoped actions with an approval and rollback path.
decision.chosenReason: This delivers automated evaluation and governance while keeping financial purchases and workload changes under organization-controlled authority.

alternatives.tradeoff: Can cause availability or financial harm when utilization evidence is stale or a workload has an unobserved constraint.
Reduces risk but leaves configured budget and governance rules dependent on manual review.

steps.phase: Define boundaries and the trust contract
steps.title: Scale the ingestion design from the stated resource floor
steps.content: The brief explicitly requires 10k+ cloud resources across accounts. It does not give account count, event rate, tenant count, or growth curve, so do not invent those values as sizing facts.

scaleTrigger.metric: Observed resource count, per-account ingestion lag, and warehouse partition/query pressure
scaleTrigger.action: Partition ingestion and analytical access by provider, tenant, and account; add independent workers only when measured backlog or query latency requires it.
scaleTrigger.impact: Improves isolation and horizontal capacity while adding cross-partition query and operational complexity.

steps.title: Land AWS billing exports
steps.content: Treat provider billing exports as source evidence and preserve their original period, account, currency, and export identity for reconciliation.

component.label: AWS Billing Export Landing
component.description: Versioned landing location for AWS cost and usage exports, retained with provider/account/period identity before normalization.

properties.purpose: Versioned landing location for AWS cost and usage exports, retained with provider/account/period identity before normalization.

component.highlightReason: Preserve the raw provider record so transformed spend can be traced back to a reproducible export.

steps.title: Land Azure billing exports
steps.content: Use the provider's corresponding billing export format, but map it into the same canonical ledger only after recording its original schema and currency semantics.

component.label: Azure Billing Export Landing
component.description: Versioned landing location for Azure Cost Management billing exports, retaining original account, period, currency, and schema metadata.

properties.purpose: Versioned landing location for Azure Cost Management billing exports, retaining original account, period, currency, and schema metadata.

component.highlightReason: Provider-specific billing fields differ; retain the source representation for reconciliation and parser upgrades.

steps.title: Land Google Cloud billing exports
steps.content: Preserve the export's billing account, project, service, SKU, usage interval, and currency fields before mapping them to canonical dimensions.

component.label: GCP Billing Export Landing
component.description: Versioned landing location for Google Cloud billing export data with original billing-account, project, service, SKU, period, and currency context.

properties.purpose: Versioned landing location for Google Cloud billing export data with original billing-account, project, service, SKU, period, and currency context.

component.highlightReason: Keep the provider's source fields intact so service and project attribution can be audited after normalization.

steps.title: Add the multi-cloud provider adapter
steps.content: No dedicated multi-cloud billing-and-resource adapter exists in the catalog, so use its supported generic custom component. Keep provider-specific authentication, schema adapters, read-only inventory, usage signals, and explicitly enabled write operations behind this replaceable boundary.

component.label: Multi-cloud Account Adapter
component.description: Provider boundary for AWS, Azure, and GCP billing export discovery, read-only resource inventory and utilization signals, and separately gated opt-in policy actions.

properties.subtitle: AWS · Azure · GCP
properties.purpose: Provider boundary for AWS, Azure, and GCP billing export discovery, read-only resource inventory and utilization signals, and separately gated opt-in policy actions.
properties.technology: AWS billing exports, Azure Cost Management, Google Cloud Billing
properties.notes: Use tenant-scoped credentials and least privilege. Writes remain disabled unless the account owner configures an allow-listed policy and explicit approval path.

component.highlightReason: Isolate provider-specific schemas and credentials while preserving the three named billing sources and a separately controlled execution boundary.

steps.title: Read AWS exports through the provider adapter
steps.content: Validate export identity and completeness before acknowledging a new billing period; retries must not create duplicate cost facts.

connection.label: AWS billing and usage records
connection.description: Discover versioned AWS export objects and pass provider/account/period metadata for idempotent parsing.

steps.title: Read Azure exports through the same contract
steps.content: Keep Azure-specific meter and resource identifiers alongside normalized fields so provider reconciliation remains possible.

connection.label: Azure billing and usage records
connection.description: Read versioned Cost Management exports and map provider fields without discarding their source identifiers.

steps.title: Read GCP exports through the same contract
steps.content: Preserve billing-account, project, service, and SKU dimensions even when some records arrive later as adjustments or credits.

connection.label: GCP billing and usage records
connection.description: Read versioned export rows and retain their original billing/project identity for later reconciliation.

steps.title: Buffer arrivals and provider retries
steps.content: Queue export notifications and inventory deltas so provider outages, backfills, and bursts do not block parsing. Use idempotency keys derived from tenant, provider, account, export identity, and record identity.

component.label: Billing & Usage Intake Queue
component.description: Durable asynchronous buffer for export-arrival notifications, inventory changes, usage signals, and retryable provider ingestion work.

properties.purpose: Durable asynchronous buffer for export-arrival notifications, inventory changes, usage signals, and retryable provider ingestion work.

component.highlightReason: Decouple provider freshness and retry behavior from normalization and analytical queries.

steps.title: Publish provider work for asynchronous ingestion
steps.content: Queue a pointer and source metadata rather than copying large billing files into a message; retry and dead-letter behavior should be observable.

connection.label: Export and usage work items
connection.description: Enqueue versioned source references and account-scoped usage events for idempotent processing.

steps.title: Normalize cost records without losing provenance
steps.content: Map provider-specific rows into a canonical fact contract: tenant, provider, account, resource, service, team tags, usage interval, currency, charge kind, estimated/final status, source revision, and adjustment lineage.

component.label: Cost & Usage Normalizer
component.description: Stateful parser and canonicalizer for provider billing exports, usage events, late adjustments, deduplication, and source-lineage metadata.

properties.purpose: Stateful parser and canonicalizer for provider billing exports, usage events, late adjustments, deduplication, and source-lineage metadata.

component.highlightReason: A shared canonical fact shape enables cross-cloud analysis while source revisions and estimate status keep the result auditable.

steps.title: Deliver buffered work to the normalizer
steps.content: Use replayable offsets or equivalent checkpoints and an idempotent sink; exactly-once claims depend on the full source-to-sink implementation, not the diagram label.

connection.label: Replayable normalization work
connection.description: Deliver provider work with retry, checkpoint, duplicate detection, and dead-letter visibility.

steps.title: Retain immutable normalized source evidence
steps.content: Use a replaceable central object-storage landing area for normalized snapshots and replay manifests. S3 is an illustrative deployment choice because the catalog requires one provider value; it is not a multi-cloud product requirement.

component.label: Normalized Cost Evidence Lake
component.description: Versioned central object store for normalized provider snapshots, replay manifests, and reconciliation evidence before analytical aggregation.

properties.purpose: Versioned central object store for normalized provider snapshots, replay manifests, and reconciliation evidence before analytical aggregation.

component.highlightReason: Retain replayable evidence independently from curated aggregates and user-facing summaries.

steps.title: Archive normalized source facts
steps.content: Keep source revision, ingestion time, and estimated-versus-final state attached so a late credit or re-export can be reconciled rather than silently overwriting history.

connection.label: Versioned normalized evidence
connection.description: Write canonical records and lineage manifests for replay, reconciliation, and audit.

steps.title: Collect resource utilization evidence
steps.content: Rightsizing needs time-series utilization and resource identity, not spend alone. Collect provider metrics through tenant-scoped integrations, preserve collection timestamps, and mark missing or stale signals explicitly.

component.label: Cross-cloud Utilization Signals
component.description: Timestamped CPU, memory, storage, network, and resource-lifecycle signals joined to tenant/account/resource identity through provider integrations.

properties.purpose: Timestamped CPU, memory, storage, network, and resource-lifecycle signals joined to tenant/account/resource identity through provider integrations.

component.highlightReason: A rightsizing suggestion must be grounded in recent utilization and must not mistake a telemetry gap for an idle resource.

steps.title: Collect provider-side signals through the adapter
steps.content: The provider adapter fans timestamped resource telemetry and inventory changes into the utilization collector. Metrics remain distinct from invoice facts; align time windows and identity but retain their source and freshness metadata.

connection.label: Provider inventory and utilization feed
connection.description: Collect timestamped cross-cloud resource metrics and lifecycle events with provider/account/resource identity and source freshness.

steps.title: Build the analytical cost and usage ledger
steps.content: Partition analytical facts around provider, tenant/account, service/resource, and usage time so team/service queries and backtests can be measured at the stated 10k+ resource floor. The brief provides no billing-history duration or event-rate number, so size storage from observed retention and growth.

component.label: Multi-cloud Cost & Usage Warehouse
component.description: Analytical store for canonical cost facts, resource utilization, tags, account/service dimensions, reconciled actuals, and forecast evaluation history.

properties.purpose: Analytical store for canonical cost facts, resource utilization, tags, account/service dimensions, reconciled actuals, and forecast evaluation history.

component.highlightReason: Separate scan-heavy analytical facts from policy OLTP state and support consistent provider, team, and service rollups.

steps.title: Load canonical facts for cross-provider analysis
steps.content: Publish idempotent canonical records and late-adjustment lineage. Consumers can then compare providers without adding unlike currencies, billing periods, or estimated and finalized costs as if they were identical.

connection.label: Canonical cost and usage facts
connection.description: Load provider-tagged cost, usage, resource, and freshness facts for analytical queries and model features.

steps.title: Create team and service cost views
steps.content: Apply explicit ownership tags and organization mappings first. Preserve allocation rules and their version so chargeback can be reproduced for a closed period.

component.label: Allocation & Showback Analytics
component.description: Versioned allocation pipeline for provider/account/service spend, explicit ownership tags, approved tag inference, and team/service showback or chargeback views.

properties.purpose: Versioned allocation pipeline for provider/account/service spend, explicit ownership tags, approved tag inference, and team/service showback or chargeback views.

component.highlightReason: Make every allocated amount traceable to a source fact and a versioned ownership rule.

steps.title: Aggregate spend by the dimensions the brief names
steps.content: Materialize or query provider, team, and service totals from canonical facts while retaining a drill-down path to account and resource evidence.

connection.label: Provider-tagged cost facts
connection.description: Aggregate canonical actual and estimated spend into auditable account, service, team, and period views.

steps.title: Profile workloads for safe comparisons
steps.content: Cluster resource usage patterns to distinguish steady services, bursty jobs, seasonal workloads, and likely idle assets. Treat clusters as evidence for review, not as proof that two resources are interchangeable.

component.label: Workload Profiling Model
component.description: Clustering model over time-series utilization and resource metadata to group workload behavior for rightsizing and commitment analysis.

properties.purpose: Clustering model over time-series utilization and resource metadata to group workload behavior for rightsizing and commitment analysis.

component.highlightReason: Use workload profiles to inform comparable analysis while preserving per-resource evidence and confidence.

steps.title: Build profiles from reconciled cost and usage history
steps.content: Join telemetry windows to billed resource identity and exclude missing or stale intervals from recommendations until enough evidence exists.

connection.label: Resource history and cost context
connection.description: Supply time-series usage, provider/resource metadata, and reconciled spend features for workload clustering.

steps.title: Use approved inference for resources missing ownership tags
steps.content: Join workload and service metadata to the allocation pipeline. Store the inference reason and confidence; route low-confidence or conflicting ownership to an explicit unallocated bucket for human review rather than silently charging a team.

connection.label: Workload and ownership evidence
connection.description: Provide profile features for approved tag inference while retaining confidence, lineage, and unresolved ownership state.

steps.title: Detect unexpected cost changes
steps.content: Score cost and usage series for unusual shifts with provider, account, service, and workload context. Keep anomaly evidence, baseline window, and model version with each alert so a spike is explainable.

component.label: Cost Anomaly Detector
component.description: Anomaly-detection model for unexpected spend and usage changes, emitting explainable evidence, baseline context, and model version.

properties.purpose: Anomaly-detection model for unexpected spend and usage changes, emitting explainable evidence, baseline context, and model version.

component.highlightReason: Identify anomalous spend or usage and make the detection evidence reviewable instead of presenting an unexplained score.

steps.title: Score anomalies against cost history
steps.content: Separate finalized billed changes from early estimated-cost alerts, then reconcile the alert when provider actuals arrive.

connection.label: Cost and usage time series
connection.description: Supply versioned provider/account/service series with actual-versus-estimated status and baseline features.

steps.title: Use fresh telemetry for early warning
steps.content: Billing exports may arrive later than the one-hour detection target. Use fresh usage or estimated-spend signals for provisional alerts, label them as estimates, and reconcile them when billing data is finalized; validate provider-specific freshness before claiming the target is met.

connection.label: Fresh usage and lifecycle signals
connection.description: Feed timestamped cross-cloud signals for early anomaly detection while preserving estimated status and source freshness.

steps.title: Surface explainable anomalies beside allocated spend
steps.content: A team should see the affected provider, service, expected baseline, observed change, and whether the amount is estimated or finalized.

connection.label: Anomaly findings with ownership context
connection.description: Attach model evidence to the relevant account, team, and service cost views for investigation.

steps.title: Define the anomaly operating point with evidence
steps.content: The brief sets a one-hour detection target but not an acceptable false-positive rate or exact start/end timestamps. Set those with users and measure end-to-end from the earliest supported source signal to a visible, actionable finding.

decision.question: How should the platform trade anomaly sensitivity against alert fatigue?
decision.chosen: Use separate, versioned policies for early estimated signals and reconciled billed anomalies; tune thresholds from reviewed outcomes and report both detection latency and false-positive rate.
decision.chosenReason: It preserves the one-hour target as a measurable objective without treating provisional estimates as booked spend or inventing an error budget.

alternatives.option: Alert on every deviation from a fixed baseline
alternatives.tradeoff: Can create alert fatigue when seasonality, credits, or normal deployment events shift spend.
May miss the stated detection window when a provider's billing export is not fresh enough.

steps.title: Trigger capacity work from measured lag, not guessed throughput
steps.content: Use the stated one-hour anomaly target as the end-to-end objective. The brief does not specify provider export freshness or ingest volume, so the source freshness distribution must be measured separately from model runtime.

scaleTrigger.metric: Source-event age, queue age, normalization lag, model-evaluation lag, and time-to-visible finding
scaleTrigger.action: Scale or isolate provider/account workers when measured lag threatens the one-hour objective; show a degraded-data warning when the upstream source itself is late.
scaleTrigger.impact: Separating ingestion from scoring contains provider-specific delays but increases operational paths and alerting responsibilities.

steps.title: Choose a defensible ownership rule
steps.content: Use deterministic tags and approved organization mappings when present. Inference may suggest an owner for untagged spend, but chargeback should not silently turn a probabilistic suggestion into a financial fact.

decision.question: What happens when a resource has no reliable team or service owner?
decision.chosen: Retain the spend in an explicit unallocated bucket, show the inferred owner and evidence separately, and require an organization-approved confidence policy before assigning chargeback.
decision.chosenReason: This preserves total spend visibility and gives owners a correction path without fabricating attribution certainty.

alternatives.option: Assign every untagged resource to the most likely team
alternatives.tradeoff: Improves apparent allocation coverage while risking incorrect financial attribution.

alternatives.option: Exclude untagged resources from team reports
alternatives.tradeoff: Understates total spend and hides the cost of missing ownership metadata.

steps.title: Estimate usage-based rightsizing candidates
steps.content: Use time-series utilization, resource family/region constraints, and observed workload profiles to produce candidate instance sizes and expected cost deltas. Keep recommendation generation separate from execution.

component.label: Rightsizing Candidate Model
component.description: Regression model over time-series utilization and provider resource metadata to rank feasible instance-size candidates with estimated savings and evidence.

properties.purpose: Regression model over time-series utilization and provider resource metadata to rank feasible instance-size candidates with estimated savings and evidence.

component.highlightReason: Recommend instance rightsizing from observed time-series usage and present an expected saving with its evidence and uncertainty.

steps.title: Feed rightsizing from cost and resource history
steps.content: Exclude resources with insufficient or stale samples and retain the reason a candidate was withheld, so silence is not confused with a verified no-opportunity result.

connection.label: Time-series usage and provider constraints
connection.description: Provide historical usage, resource catalog, charge rates, and workload metadata for candidate scoring.

steps.title: Validate candidates against fresh telemetry
steps.content: A low average can hide peaks or a recent workload change. Include peak/percentile context selected with operators and suppress a recommendation when the evidence window is incomplete.

connection.label: Fresh utilization and lifecycle evidence
connection.description: Supply timestamped telemetry and staleness markers to validate candidate sizes against actual workload behavior.

steps.title: Optimize reserved-instance and savings-plan coverage
steps.content: Use a constrained portfolio optimizer to compare eligible usage, rates, term, flexibility, and demand uncertainty. The catalog has no dedicated RI/SP optimizer, so the general backend service is the closest supported analog; the optimization domain logic remains explicit in its description.

component.label: Commitment Portfolio Optimizer
component.description: Constrained what-if optimizer for provider-specific reserved-instance and savings-plan coverage, eligibility, term, flexibility, utilization risk, and estimated net savings.

properties.purpose: Constrained what-if optimizer for provider-specific reserved-instance and savings-plan coverage, eligibility, term, flexibility, utilization risk, and estimated net savings.

component.highlightReason: Compare commitment alternatives as a portfolio and expose underutilization risk rather than maximizing nominal discount in isolation.

steps.title: Combine rightsizing candidates with commitment planning
steps.content: A rightsizing decision can change the demand base used for a commitment plan. Compare both sequences in what-if scenarios and show assumptions rather than double-counting savings.

connection.label: Feasible post-rightsize demand
connection.description: Pass candidate demand profiles and estimated deltas to the commitment portfolio optimizer for joint scenario evaluation.

steps.title: Compare provider prices and commitment coverage
steps.content: Apply each provider's actual eligibility and pricing rules to the scenario. Keep one-off credits, exchange rates, term assumptions, and coverage gaps visible so unlike offers are not compared as equivalent.

connection.label: Historical demand and rate evidence
connection.description: Supply provider-specific usage history, current rate inputs, and commitment coverage for pricing-model what-if analysis.

steps.title: Forecast spend over an agreed horizon
steps.content: Train or evaluate a time-series forecast by team and service, with seasonality and known business events where available. The brief gives an accuracy target but does not define forecast horizon, cadence, or aggregation currency; those remain product decisions.

component.label: Team & Service Cost Forecaster
component.description: Time-series forecasting model for future cloud costs by team and service, with backtest evidence, data freshness, and uncertainty context.

properties.purpose: Time-series forecasting model for future cloud costs by team and service, with backtest evidence, data freshness, and uncertainty context.

component.highlightReason: Produce the requested forward view with explicit backtest and uncertainty evidence rather than implying that a model name guarantees accuracy.

steps.title: Train and backtest against reconciled actuals
steps.content: Use time-ordered evaluation to avoid training on future information. Compare the agreed error metric across teams/services and report sparse-history segments separately.

connection.label: Reconciled team and service history
connection.description: Supply time-series actuals, allocation dimensions, and historical forecast evaluation data.

steps.title: Expose forecasts alongside allocated spend
steps.content: Display actuals, estimates, and forecast values distinctly. Allow drill-down to the team/service allocation rule and backtest segment that produced each forecast.

connection.label: Forecasts by team and service
connection.description: Join forecast outputs with allocation dimensions and present uncertainty and evaluation context in cost views.

steps.title: Keep commitment planning separate from purchasing
steps.content: Optimizing reserved-instance and savings-plan coverage is not the same as placing a financial order. The architecture produces candidate portfolios, projected utilization, and what-if comparisons; purchase authority stays with the account owner unless explicitly enabled.

decision.question: Should the optimizer buy a commitment when its modeled savings are positive?
decision.chosen: Return ranked, explainable coverage scenarios for review; require explicit account-level authorization and policy approval before any purchase API call.
decision.chosenReason: Provider terms and future demand create financial lock-in risk, and the brief does not authorize autonomous purchases.

alternatives.option: Automatically purchase the highest predicted-savings plan
alternatives.tradeoff: Can turn forecast error or an eligibility mismatch into an underutilized commitment.

alternatives.option: Show only current coverage with no scenarios
alternatives.tradeoff: Avoids execution risk but does not deliver the requested optimization or what-if comparison.

steps.title: Treat the forecast threshold as a backtest gate
steps.content: The stated target is forecast accuracy within 10%. Define its error metric, horizon, and evaluation population with users before release; none is specified in the brief.

scaleTrigger.metric: Time-ordered forecast error against reconciled actuals, segmented by team, service, provider, and agreed horizon
scaleTrigger.action: Keep a baseline forecast and flag segments outside the agreed 10% target; add model complexity only when backtests show a repeatable improvement.
scaleTrigger.impact: Segmented evaluation exposes weak data coverage and avoids hiding poor cohorts inside a favorable global average.

steps.title: Define what recommendation accuracy means
steps.content: The brief says cost-savings recommendation accuracy must exceed 90%, but does not specify whether accuracy means realized savings, eligibility precision, predicted-versus-realized error, or another measure. Agree a label and observation window before presenting a pass/fail badge.

decision.question: How should recommendation quality be evaluated against the stated threshold?
decision.chosen: Version a FinOps-approved metric; compare predicted benefit and eligibility with reviewed outcomes after implementation, and publish coverage, denominator, and confidence alongside the measured result.
decision.chosenReason: A visible numerator, denominator, and outcome definition make the above-90% target auditable and prevent a model score from masquerading as realized savings.

alternatives.option: Use model confidence as recommendation accuracy
alternatives.tradeoff: Confidence is not evidence that a recommendation is feasible or saved the predicted amount.
Can bias the metric toward easy cases and hide incorrect recommendations that were rejected.

steps.title: Evaluate automated cost-governance policies
steps.content: Evaluate versioned rules against proposed changes and forecasts: account/team scope, budget or policy condition, allowed action class, approval requirement, and effective period. A denied or unresolved action is an explicit outcome, not a silent drop.

component.label: Cost Governance Policy Engine
component.description: Deterministic evaluator for versioned tenant/account cost policies, budgets, recommendation eligibility, approval requirements, and opt-in automated actions.

properties.purpose: Deterministic evaluator for versioned tenant/account cost policies, budgets, recommendation eligibility, approval requirements, and opt-in automated actions.

component.highlightReason: Make automated governance explicit, versioned, and reviewable while separating a policy decision from authority to mutate cloud resources.

steps.title: Apply policy to optimization proposals
steps.content: Require the policy result to retain the recommendation/model versions and evidence IDs that were evaluated, so a later re-run cannot rewrite the original decision.

connection.label: Commitment scenarios for policy review
connection.description: Submit eligible coverage scenarios, projected savings, utilization risk, and evidence lineage for governance evaluation.

steps.title: Check forecasts against team and service policy
steps.content: Forecast-based governance should identify the forecast horizon and uncertainty and avoid treating a low-confidence projection as a booked overrun.

connection.label: Forecast evidence for budget policies
connection.description: Evaluate forecasted team/service spend with model version, actual-versus-estimated status, and uncertainty context.

steps.title: Persist every policy outcome
steps.content: Record allow, deny, needs-approval, and stale-evidence outcomes with the policy version, actor, scope, and reason. Retries must be idempotent and must not repeat a provider-side action.

connection.label: Versioned governance decisions
connection.description: Persist policy evaluation, approval status, audit references, and idempotency state for each recommendation.

steps.title: Gate optional provider-side actions
steps.content: Keep provider writes disabled unless an organization owner configures credentials, action scopes, approvals, and rollback/compensation behavior. RI/SP purchase calls require separate financial authorization from reversible resource changes.

connection.label: Explicitly authorized provider action
connection.description: Send only allow-listed, approved actions with tenant/account scope, idempotency key, and recorded policy decision.

steps.title: Show policy state next to allocated outcomes
steps.content: Expose pending approval, applied, denied, and measured-after-action states beside the team's cost view; do not label a proposed saving as realized savings.

connection.label: Governance and realized-outcome status
connection.description: Join versioned policy outcomes and later measured savings to the owning team/service allocation view.

steps.title: Serve reviewed allocations and forecasts to users
steps.content: The API returns tenant-authorized team/service views with source freshness, actual/estimate/forecast status, allocation provenance, recommendation evidence, and policy outcome.

connection.label: Auditable team and service cost views
connection.description: Serve allocated spend, forecast context, anomaly findings, and recommendation/policy state to authorized workspace requests.

steps.title: Keep drill-downs tied to the analytical evidence
steps.content: Apply tenant and account filters before analytical reads and carry them through every join; never rely on the browser to enforce data isolation.

connection.label: Authorized cost evidence and drill-downs
connection.description: Query scoped analytical facts and provenance for report details, reconciliation, and recommendation evidence.

steps.title: Release only against measured evidence
steps.content: The graph provides paths for the supplied requirements; it does not prove them. Before release, measure recommendation accuracy above 90% using the agreed outcome definition, anomaly detection within 1 hour including provider source freshness, support for AWS/Azure/GCP billing data, operation at 10k+ resources across accounts, and forecast accuracy within 10% using the agreed horizon and metric. Validate tenant isolation, adjustment reconciliation, untagged-cost review, and opt-in action safety with representative data. Keep a target marked unverified whenever the evidence is missing.
